# Where the Codex copies live, and a clarify decision corrected

Slice 1 hit something the clarify record got wrong. The decision said the
generated Codex agent files are committed at `.codex/agents/` because
"committing them is what lets doctor's drift check cover all four agent copies
rather than two". Two things about that were wrong.

**The reason was wrong.** `agents.drift` reads the working tree, not the index,
so doctor checks all four copies whether or not git tracks them. What committing
actually buys is what the skill copies buy: a fresh clone has the two agents
before its first sync, and `doctor` does not refuse on a clone for a file that
has never been generated on it.

**`.codex/` is ignored, by an earlier decision.** SEEN-102 put it in
`.gitignore` because repowise writes editor and agent wiring there that points at
each machine's own absolute paths, and `.codex/config.toml` on this machine
indeed carries `cwd = "/Users/ruudvanengelenhoven/Development/seene"`. That
reason does not reach the generated agent files, which carry no path at all, so
the rule is narrowed rather than reversed: `.codex/*` with `!.codex/agents/`.
`config.toml` stays out.

**The cap cannot be tested.** The same decision named `[agents] max_depth = 1` in
`.codex/config.toml`, and that file is untracked on purpose, so it is absent in
CI and on every other clone. The setting is made on this machine, the test that
asserted it has been removed rather than left to pass here and fail everywhere
else, and the cap belongs in the skill, which slice 4 changes and which is
generated, committed and checked by doctor.

Nothing about the criteria changed. What changed is one line of `.gitignore`, one
test that could not hold, and a decision whose reason now matches what the code
actually does.
